newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Traders divided over India's Dec diesel imports.
newsitem.headline: Traders divided over India's Dec diesel imports.

text.p: Offers to state-owned Indian Oil Corp's (IOC) tender to buy high speed diesel for December delivery were within market expectations but players' estimates of the volume IOC would buy were mixed.
Some traders said on Friday that IOC will buy 600,000-tonnes but others said it would be much lesser.
"I have heard everthing from 200,000 tonnes to 600,000 tonnes today. I think they will buy 400,000 tonnes," one trader said.
Players who cited the higher import volumes pointed to the firmer swaps prices as evidence of this. November swaps rose to trade at $30.25, up from Thursday's close of $29.90/29.85.
Offer prices to the tender were within market expectations.
The offer for 0.5-percent sulphur diesel to the east coast ranged between $2.50 and $2.80 premium to MidEast spot quotes, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis.
Cargoes for delivery to the west coast were seen at $1.90-2.30 per barrel over MidEast quotes, c-and-f.
IOC cancelled its last tender to buy diesel for arrival in November and in October it bought a mere 120,000 tonnes due to port congestions.
